'''Ram Prakash''' (5 October 1939 – 13 December 2023) was a Vedic scholar, author, educationist and a member of the  [[Parliament of India]] representing [[Haryana]] in the [[Rajya Sabha]], the upper house of the [[Indian Parliament]] from 2007 to 2014.

He authored and edited books on Vedic philosophy and was the second Chairperson of the 'Centre for Studies in Civilizations'. He was a professor of Chemistry, a Fulbright scholar, and the Chancellor of Gurukula Kangri University, Haridwar.<ref>http://gkv.ac.in/fwd/notification%20scan%20english.jpg. {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130823093408/http://gkv.ac.in/fwd/notification%20scan%20english.jpg |date=23 August 2013 }}</ref>

==Early life==
Ram Prakash, son of Sh. Prabhu Dayal, was born on 5 October 1939, in the village of Tangore, [[Kurukshetra]] district of Haryana (formerly [[Punjab, India|Punjab]]), India, of OBC (Other Backward Castes).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/2005/20051013/haryana.htm|title = The Tribune, Chandigarh, India - Haryana}}</ref> Prakash gained his MSc and PhD degrees in [[Chemistry]] from the [[Panjab University, Chandigarh|Punjab University]], [[Chandigarh]], and subsequently taught at the institution.<ref>[http://164.100.24.167:8080/members/website/Mainweb.asp?mpcode=2041 Profile on Rajya Sabha website] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930181545/http://164.100.24.167:8080/members/website/Mainweb.asp?mpcode=2041 |date=30 September 2007 }}</ref> Later, he joined the new [[Kurukshetra University]] as the Pro-Vice Chancellor for a while.

==Politics==
Prakash entered politics in 1990–1991 and in 1999 won the local elections on an [[Indian National Congress]] (INC) party ticket. Being close to the Haryana [[Chief Minister]], [[Bhupinder Singh Hooda]], he eventually rose to be Working President of the INC party in Haryana and was elevated to the [[Rajya Sabha]] in 2007.

==Personal life and death==
In 1966 Prakash married SM. Vijay Kumari, and had two sons by his marriage. He lived mostly in Kurukshetra, Haryana, and also at [[New Delhi]].

Ram Prakash died on 13 December 2023, at the age of 84.<ref>[https://www.ptinews.com/news/national/former-haryana-congress-chief-ram-prakash-passes-away/706048.html Former Haryana Congress chief Ram Prakash passes away]</ref>
